papers.title: Modulating the WNK1-SPAK/OSR1-KCC2 Pathway: Acupuncture's Therapeutic Potential in Mitigating Muscle Hypertonia in Ischemic Stroke Rats.
papers.authors: Sun TY, Ma LX, Zhang WX, Lu SB, Xiu JY, Chen MY
papers.abstract: This study investigated the therapeutic effects of acupuncture on post-stroke muscle hypertonia (PSMH) in rats, focusing on the WNK1-SPAK/OSR1-KCC2 pathway to elucidate its underlying mechanisms and support clinical translation. Behavioral, electrophysiological, TTC staining, AChE staining, and transmission electron microscope analyses were used to assess the efficacy of acupuncture. RT-qPCR, Western blot, and immunofluorescence were used to evaluate the expression of the medullary WNK1-SPAK/OSR1-KCC2 pathway. Pharmacological modulation using WNK463 and Gabazine suggested the involvement of WNK kinase activity. Acupuncture reduced neurological deficits and spasticity, enhanced motor recovery, suppressed spinal motor neuron hyperexcitability, and ameliorated neuromuscular dysfunction and muscular structural abnormality. Mechanistically, it downregulated WNK1, SPAK, and OSR1 and increased membrane KCC2 expression in the medulla oblongata. WNK463 partially mimicked acupuncture's effects, while Gabazine partially reversed them. Acupuncture alleviates muscle hypertonia and enhances locomotor recovery in rats with PSMH, potentially by inhibiting the medullary WNK1-SPAK/OSR1 pathway and thereby upregulating KCC2 expression and membrane localization.

papers.title: Low-dose histrelin for ovulation induction in mares: a partially randomized crossover pilot study.
papers.authors: de Barros Fogagnoli L, Jose KCA, Weckl R, Mota CMO, Fernandes MO, Machado RC et al.
papers.abstract: This partially randomized crossover pilot study evaluated reduced doses of histrelin for ovulation induction in mares and compared intramuscular (IM) administration with pharmacopuncture at the Bai-hui and Yan-chi acupoints. Eleven mares were enrolled, of which nine completed all eight protocols and were included in the analyses. The protocols comprised 250 µg histrelin IM (standard dose), 75 µg IM, 25 µg IM, no intervention, saline at Bai-hui, saline at Yan-chi, 25 µg histrelin at Bai-hui, and 25 µg histrelin at Yan-chi. Ovulation was assessed by transrectal ultrasonography at scheduled examinations until detected, with ovulation within 48 h as the primary outcome. Ovulations first detected at 24 h were excluded from the primary analysis. Ovulation within 48 h occurred in 88.9% (8/9) of observations with 250 µg IM, 87.5% (7/8) with 75 µg IM, 87.5% (7/8) with 25 µg IM, 37.5% (3/8) with no intervention, 50.0% (3/6) with saline at Bai-hui, 100% (9/9) with 25 µg histrelin at Bai-hui, 12.5% (1/8) with saline at Yan-chi, and 87.5% (7/8) with 25 µg histrelin at Yan-chi. Exact 95% confidence intervals were wide, reflecting the small sample size. Exploratory pairwise comparisons with the no-intervention protocol were performed without adjustment for multiple comparisons and should be interpreted cautiously. The findings provide preliminary evidence that reduced histrelin doses, including 25 µg, may induce ovulation within 48 h in mares. However, this study did not demonstrate an advantage of pharmacopuncture over IM administration of the same reduced dose. Larger, fully randomized studies are required to confirm the efficacy of reduced-dose histrelin and determine whether administration at specific acupoints provides any additional effect.

papers.title: Risk-Oriented Clinical Management and Observed Safety Outcomes of Acupuncture in Patients at Risk of Metal Allergy: A Single-Center Retrospective Case Series.
papers.journal: Journal of integrative and complementary medicine
papers.authors: Fujita Y, Kikuchi T, Yamaguchi S, Horibe G, Ibata S, Sekiya T et al.
papers.abstract:
Acupuncture is widely used in complementary and integrative medicine. Because acupuncture needles are primarily made of stainless steel, patients at risk of metal allergy require careful management. However, evidence regarding risk-oriented clinical management and observed safety outcomes remains limited. This study aimed to describe risk-oriented clinical management and observed safety outcomes in routine acupuncture practice, including those at risk of metal allergy.
This single-center retrospective case series included consecutive new patients receiving acupuncture over 1 year. Electronic medical records were reviewed for metal allergy risk, clinical management, and adverse events. Patients were classified as at risk of metal allergy based on documented history, self-reported symptoms, or clinical findings. Clinical management was individualized based on risk assessment, clinical judgment, and patient preferences. Safety outcomes included metal contact allergic reactions, systemic metal allergy reactions, and other serious adverse events.
Among 230 patients, 23 (10.0%) were classified as at risk of metal allergy. Clinical management included risk assessment, stepwise and minimally invasive approaches, consideration of alternative materials, and post-treatment monitoring. Among 22 patients, 220 treatment sessions were performed. No cases of metal contact allergic reactions, systemic metal allergy reactions, or other serious adverse events were observed. Likewise, no such adverse events were observed in the overall study population.
This study provides a practice-based description of risk-oriented clinical management and observed safety outcomes in patients receiving acupuncture, including those at risk of metal allergy. The findings illustrate how patients at risk of metal allergy were assessed and managed in routine acupuncture practice, while the absence of observed adverse events should be interpreted cautiously given the limited sample size and observational study design.

papers.title: Tongsai Granules Ameliorate Airway Mucus Hypersecretion in AECOPD by Remodeling LIPA-Driven Ceramide Metabolism.
papers.authors: Cheng M, Li K, Zhang Z, Xin N, Liu X, Du Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Tongsai Granules (TSG) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula traditionally used for the treatment of acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) with phlegm-heat obstructing lung syndrome, a condition characterized by cough, excessive sputum production, and dyspnea; however, its underlying therapeutic mechanisms remain unclear.
To investigate the mechanisms by which TSG alleviates airway mucus hypersecretion in AECOPD through regulation of the LIPA/ceramide axis.
A murine AECOPD model and airway epithelial cells were used. Proteomic and lipidomic analyses, molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), and LIPA overexpression and knockdown assays were performed.
TSG improved pulmonary function, attenuated lung injury and inflammation, and suppressed MUC5AC expression in AECOPD mice. Multi-omics analyses showed that TSG regulated lipid metabolism and reduced triglyceride and ceramide accumulation while downregulating lysosomal acid lipase A (LIPA). Several serum-exposed constituents of TSG inhibited MUC5AC expression. Bergenin (BER) was selected as a representative bioactive constituent for subsequent target-identification and mechanistic studies. Molecular docking, SPR, and DARTS assays demonstrated direct interaction between BER and LIPA. LIPA knockdown suppressed MUC5AC expression, whereas LIPA overexpression attenuated the inhibitory effect of BER. Moreover, exogenous ceramide reversed BER-mediated suppression of MUC5AC.
TSG alleviates airway mucus hypersecretion in AECOPD by targeting the LIPA/ceramide axis. Bergenin directly targets LIPA to regulate lipid metabolism and suppress MUC5AC overexpression.

papers.title: Short-term Efficacy of massage and related treatments for Ankylosing Spondylitis: A Systematic Review and Meta Analysis.
papers.authors: Shengyang Y, Siqi L, Yangming X, Junjie Z, Bowen Z, Qingguang Z et al.
papers.abstract:
Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory rheumatic disease causing significant pain, stiffness, and functional impairment. Conventional treatments are limited by adverse events and poor efficacy for axial manifestations, leading AS patients to seek complementary therapies such as massage. However, no systematic reviews or meta-analyses have synthesized evidence on massage for AS, leaving its efficacy unconfirmed.
From inception to July 5, 2025, a comprehensive literature search was conducted using eight electronic databases to identify randomized controlled trials of massage and related treatments for AS. Risk of bias was assessed via Cochrane RoB 2, and data was synthesized using Review Manager 5.4. Subgroup analysis was performed according to the different intervention methods. The I2 statistic was used to assess the heterogeneity.
Seventeen RCTs involving 1,687 patients were included. Meta-analysis demonstrated that massage significantly improved disease activity (Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index [BASDAI]: SMD = -1.09, 95% CI: -1.38 to -0.80, P < 0.001), physical function (Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index [BASFI]: SMD = -1.00, 95% CI: -1.33 to -0.67, P < 0.001), spinal pain (Visual Analog Scale [VAS-pain]: MD = -1.43, 95% CI: -1.80 to -1.05, P < 0.001), and inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate [ESR]: MD = -3.58, 95% CI: -4.71 to -2.99, P < 0.001; C-reactive protein [CRP]: SMD = -0.73, 95% CI: -1.03 to -0.43, P < 0.001) compared to control groups. Subgroup analysis suggested that massage alone might be more effective than massage combined with other therapies like acupuncture. Significant heterogeneity was observed, attributable to variations in massage techniques and protocols. Of note, the long-term efficacy of massage was not evaluated in this review, as no included studies provided follow‑up beyond the treatment period.
Massage and related treatments are effective in alleviating disease activity, improving physical function, reducing pain, and lowering inflammation in patients with ankylosing spondylitis. It can be considered as a beneficial non-pharmacological adjunct for AS. However, these findings must be interpreted with caution due to several limitations inherent in the included studies, including methodological flaws, small sample sizes, inconsistent treatment protocols, and insufficient statistical precision. Moreover, blinding was not feasible in massage therapy, which precludes exclusion of potential placebo or observer effects. Therefore, future high‑quality, standardized, and longitudinal RCTs are warranted to confirm the role of massage in evidence‑based AS management.

papers.title: Therapeutic effects of Stemona japonica extract against Mycoplasma gallisepticum infection: Association with suppression of NF-κB-mediated inflammatory response.
papers.authors: Yao W, Liang X, Zhang Z, Li X, Ma X, Zhao Z et al.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma gallisepticum (MG) is the primary causative agent of chronic respiratory disease (CRD) in chickens, causing massive economic losses to the global poultry industry. The widespread emergence of antibiotic-resistant MG strains has created an urgent need for safe and effective alternative therapies. Stemona japonica (Baibu), a traditional Chinese medicine with well-documented antitussive and anti-inflammatory properties, has not been systematically evaluated for its anti-MG activity. This study investigated the therapeutic effects of S. japonica extract against MG infection both in vitro and in vivo, and elucidated its underlying molecular mechanisms. In chicken respiratory epithelial cells, S. japonica extract significantly alleviated MG-induced cellular injury, improved cell viability, reduced apoptosis, and dose-dependently downregulated the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IFN-γ). Mechanistically, S. japonica suppressed MG-induced activation of the NF-κB signaling pathway by inhibiting the phosphorylation and degradation of IκBα and subsequent phosphorylation of p65. In a chicken MG infection model, S. japonica treatment significantly alleviated clinical symptoms, reduced body weight loss and mortality, elevated serum IgG and IgA levels, and attenuated lung pathological damage. Transcriptome sequencing further confirmed that S. japonica reversed MG-induced gene expression changes, with differentially expressed genes highly enriched in NF-κB, TNF, and cytokine-receptor interaction pathways. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that S. japonica exerts potent therapeutic effects against MG infection, which is associated with suppression of NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses and enhancement of host humoral immunity. This study provides a scientific basis for the development of S. japonica as a promising alternative agent for the treatment of CRD in poultry.

papers.title: Functionalized Chinese Medicine-Derived Quercetin Carbon Dots for the Treatment of Osteoporosis.
papers.authors: Gan Q, Zhang Y, Wang J, Xue P, Fu Y, Yuan Y
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) compound formulas are widely employed in the clinical management of osteoporosis; however, their principal bioactive constituents and primary molecular targets remain poorly characterized. Consequently, there is an urgent need for systematic functional exploration of TCM-derived chemicals. In this study, we applied a network pharmacology-based approach to screen four canonical TCM compound prescriptions for antiosteoporotic compounds, identifying a total of 20 candidate molecules. Among these, quercetin was selected as a lead compound for the synthesis of biologically active carbon dots (CDs), which were then integrated with mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) to construct a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanocarrier system. In vitro cellular assays demonstrated that both the quercetin-derived CDs and the drug-loaded nanocarriers exhibited excellent cytocompatibility, robust osteogenic-promoting activity, and potent osteoclast-inhibitory effects. Collectively, our findings underscore the utility of network pharmacology in identifying quercetin as a promising TCM-derived lead compound for osteoporosis intervention, and the rational functionalization strategy developed herein provides a valuable paradigm for advancing the therapeutic application of TCM-derived chemicals in bone metabolic disorders.

papers.title: Integrating emerging preservation strategies in cardiac transplantation: From nanotherapeutic frontiers to clinical translation.
papers.authors: Wang H, Wang J, Deng W, Jin F, Lin C
papers.abstract: Hypothermic preservation remains a critical bottleneck in heart transplantation, primarily due to the exacerbation of ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) and tightly restricted organ viability windows. Addressing this global clinical crisis requires a departure from traditional monotherapies. This review critically appraises-rather than merely synthesizes-three multidisciplinary advancements: (1) preservation solutions supplemented with nanotherapeutics, with explicit distinction between proof-of-concept, small-animal, and clinically translatable evidence; (2) technological transitions from static cold storage (SCS) to ex vivo heart perfusion (EVHP) and nanowarming-assisted cryopreservation; and (3) bioactive compounds derived from Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), evaluated through a SWOT framework that acknowledges phytochemical variability and the paucity of clinical transplantation data. We further examine the emerging-but currently nascent and largely speculative---role of artificial intelligence in perfusion decision support. We emphasize that these three domains are not evidentially equivalent: perfusion technology is clinically implemented, pharmacological and nanotherapeutic adjuncts remain predominantly preclinical, and AI applications in cardiac preservation are currently confined to retrospective outcome modelling, with no published closed-loop perfusion control in clinical practice.

papers.title: Non-antibiotic interventions to prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in women: overview of systematic reviews of randomised controlled trials.
papers.journal: The British journal of general practice : the journal of the Royal College of General Practitioners
papers.authors: Santer M, Miller S, Fraser S, Francis N, Lown M, Becque T et al.
papers.abstract:
Recurrent urinary tract infections (rUTIs), that is, ≥2 urinary tract infections (UTIs) in the past 6 months or ≥3 in the past 12 months, are common, have a substantial impact on quality of life, and cause major antibiotic use.
To identify non-antibiotic interventions for prevention of rUTIs that have been assessed in systematic reviews, exploring their effectiveness, acceptability, and adherence.
An overview of systematic reviews of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on non-pharmaceutical and pharmaceutical (non-antibiotic) interventions for preventing rUTIs in women.
Medline, Embase, CINAHL, Google Scholar, and Cochrane from January 2014 to May 2025 were searched for systematic reviews of RCTs assessing the effectiveness of community-based non-antibiotic interventions for preventing UTI in women aged ≥16 years with rUTIs. Studies in intensive care units, relating to people with indwelling catheters, or comparing different oral antibiotic regimens were excluded. There were no limitations regarding outcome measures or language.
In total, 27 systematic reviews met inclusion criteria evaluating probiotics (n = 9), D-mannose (n = 7), vaginal oestrogen (n = 7), cranberry (n = 6), methenamine hippurate (n = 3), herbal medicine (n = 3), increased fluid intake (n = 2), systemic oestrogen (n = 4), acupuncture (n = 2), and vaccines (n = 2). Eight examined combination strategies. Cranberry and methenamine hippurate use are supported by systematic reviews, as is vaginal oestrogen among postmenopausal women, although questions remain around dose, duration, and treatment adherence. Reviews of probiotics, D-mannose, herbal medicine, acupuncture, and vaccines concluded that stronger evidence is needed. Increased fluid intake benefits women with low intake, but further research is needed on optimal intake. There was little information on treatment adherence or acceptability for many interventions.
For effective interventions, questions remain about promoting adherence (vaginal oestrogen), or optimal preparation (cranberry), or duration (methenamine). For other interventions a stronger evidence base is needed.

papers.title: A Feasible 1H-NMR Quantification Method of Indicator Compounds in Microwave-Processed Reynoutria multiflora Radix and Its Decoction.
papers.authors: Li HZ, Phan HN, Jhang ZH, Chen GF, Yang ML, Wu TS et al.
papers.abstract: Reynoutria multiflora (Thunb.) Moldenke is a commonly used herbal drug in traditional Chinese medicine. Prior literature has indicated that R. multiflora possesses broadband pharmacological activities. According to Taiwan Herbal Pharmacopeia (IV) and previous reports, the dominant components of R. multiflora were 2,3,5,4'-tetrahydroxystilbene-2-O-β-D-glucopyranoside (THSG) (1) and free anthraquinones such as emodin (2), physcion (3), and rhein (4), which played pivotal roles in the pharmacological effects of herbs. However, the standard analytic method with HPLC-UV took much time to prepare samples and calibration curves based on the standard substances. In this study, a rapid quantitative 1H-NMR analytic method has been developed, which can quantify the indicator compounds in R. multiflora samples. The method validation data demonstrated the good accuracy and precision of this qNMR method. The feasible analytical method can monitor the contents of indicator compounds in both raw and processed herbs. In addition, this method could be applied to analyze the indicator compounds in the decoction Qi Bao Mei Ran Dan successfully. These results all supported the proposed method as a useful tool for quality control of R. multiflora herbal materials and decoctions. With further refinement, this method could serve as a reference for future standard methods in pharmacopoeias.
papers.title_ko: 마이크로웨이브 처리한 하수오 뿌리와 그 탕액의 지표 성분을 정량하는 1H-NMR 방법

summary.question: 마이크로웨이브 처리한 Reynoutria multiflora Radix와 탕액에서 지표 성분을 신속하게 정량할 수 있는 1H-NMR 방법이 가능한가를 평가했다.
summary.methods: 하수오 원료와 가공품, 그리고 탕액의 지표 성분을 대상으로 1H-NMR 정량법(qNMR)을 개발하고 정확도와 정밀도를 검증한 분석 연구이다.
summary.results: 개발한 qNMR 방법은 좋은 정확도와 정밀도를 보였고, 원료·가공 약재와 Qi Bao Mei Ran Dan 탕액의 지표 성분 함량을 성공적으로 측정했다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 본 연구는 하수오 약재와 탕액의 품질관리에 qNMR이 유용할 수 있음을 시사하지만, 표준 분석법으로의 일반화에는 추가 검증이 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 임상효과가 아니라 분석법 검증 연구이며, 광범위한 표준법 적용을 위해서는 추가적인 정련과 검증이 필요하다.

pico.p: Reynoutria multiflora 원료, 마이크로웨이브 가공 약재, 그리고 관련 탕액
pico.o: 지표 성분(THSG, emodin, physcion, rhein) 정량과 품질관리 가능성
